beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! I'm so happy you're here.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, we folded shapes to find lines of symmetry, and finished patterns, like Riya's rangoli.
beats.caption: Last time: symmetry and patterns

beats.vo: Today is chapter four of Shapes, Grids and Coordinates. It's called, Angles and Turns!
beats.caption: Chapter 4 · Angles and Turns

beats.vo: By the end, you'll turn exactly like a coding robot. Let's spin into it!
beats.caption: Turn like a coding robot!

beats.vo: Picture this. It's morning assembly at school. Meet Arjun! He's standing in line, and the PT sir is calling out commands.
beats.caption: Meet Arjun at morning assembly

beats.vo: Right turn! Arjun swings round, to face his right side.
beats.caption: "Right turn!"

beats.vo: Then sir shouts, About turn! And Arjun spins round, to face the opposite way.
beats.caption: "About turn!" Now he faces the other way

beats.vo: Here's a question. Did Arjun walk anywhere? Think about it.
beats.caption: Did Arjun walk anywhere? Think!

beats.vo: No! His feet stayed on the same spot. He only changed the way he was facing. And that's exactly what a turn is.
beats.caption: Same spot! Only the way he faces changed

beats.vo: A turn means changing the way you face, without moving from your spot.
beats.caption: Turn: change the way you face, stay on the spot

beats.vo: How much you turn is called an angle. We measure angles in degrees. When you see a tiny circle after a number, it means degrees.
beats.caption: How much you turn = an angle, in degrees (°)

beats.vo: Spin all the way round, until you face the same way again. That's a full turn. And a full turn is three hundred and sixty degrees.
beats.caption: All the way round = full turn = 360°

beats.vo: Now cut that full turn into four equal parts. One part is a quarter turn. It makes a square corner, just like the corner of your notebook.
beats.caption: Quarter turn: a square corner

beats.vo: A quarter turn is ninety degrees. That's the turn Arjun makes when sir says, right turn!
beats.caption: Quarter turn = 90°

beats.vo: Look around you. Square corners are everywhere! The corner of a door, a window, even a carrom board. Each one is a quarter turn, ninety degrees.
beats.caption: Square corners everywhere: 90°

beats.vo: You can see it on a clock, too. When the minute hand moves from twelve to three, it makes a quarter turn. Ninety degrees!
beats.caption: Clock: 12 → 3 is a quarter turn (90°)

beats.vo: So, what do two quarter turns make? Ninety, plus ninety, is one hundred and eighty degrees. That's a half turn.
beats.caption: 2 quarter turns = 90° + 90° = 180°

beats.vo: After a half turn, you face the opposite way. That was Arjun's about turn! On the clock, twelve to six is a half turn.
beats.caption: Half turn: face the opposite way · 12 → 6

beats.vo: Three quarter turns make two hundred and seventy degrees. Almost all the way round! Like the minute hand going from twelve, to three, to six, to nine.
beats.caption: 3 quarter turns = 270° · 12 → 9

beats.vo: And four quarter turns? Ninety, ninety, ninety, ninety. That's three hundred and sixty degrees, a full turn. You're back, facing the same way you started!
beats.caption: 4 quarter turns = 360° = full turn!

beats.vo: To keep track of turns, we use four directions. North, east, south, and west. On a map, north is at the top, south is at the bottom, east is on the right, and west is on the left.
beats.caption: Four directions: North, East, South, West

beats.vo: A right turn goes clockwise. That's the same way a clock's hands move. Turning right, you go north, then east, then south, then west.
beats.caption: Right turn = clockwise: N → E → S → W

beats.vo: A left turn goes the other way. We call it anticlockwise. Turning left, you go north, then west, then south, then east.
beats.caption: Left turn = anticlockwise: N → W → S → E

beats.vo: Here's a trick to remember the clockwise order. Never Eat Soggy Wheat! North, east, south, west.
beats.caption: Never Eat Soggy Wheat → N, E, S, W

beats.vo: Game time! Arjun is standing in the middle of the school ground, facing north.
beats.caption: Game time! Arjun faces north

beats.vo: One quarter turn right. Which way is he facing now?
beats.caption: Facing north. 1 quarter turn right → ?

beats.vo: East! Right is clockwise, so north goes to east.
beats.caption: East! Right is clockwise

beats.vo: Now Arjun faces east, and makes one quarter turn left. Which way now? Think carefully.
beats.caption: Facing east. 1 quarter turn left → ?

beats.vo: North! Left is anticlockwise, so from east, he turns back to north.
beats.caption: North! Left is anticlockwise

beats.vo: Tricky one. He faces north, and makes three quarter turns right. Count them!
beats.caption: Facing north. 3 quarter turns right → ?

beats.vo: One, east. Two, south. Three, west! He's facing west. Three quarter turns is two hundred and seventy degrees.
beats.caption: West! N → E → S → W is 270°

beats.vo: Arjun's friend Kavya says, turn right ninety means a quarter turn anticlockwise. Hmm. Is she right? What do you think?
beats.caption: "Turn right 90° is anticlockwise." True?

beats.vo: Not quite! A right turn is clockwise, the same way a clock's hands move. Anticlockwise is a left turn.
beats.caption: False! Right turn = clockwise

beats.vo: Turns are super important in coding. In block coding, a robot turtle obeys commands like, turn right ninety.
beats.caption: Coding: "turn right 90"

beats.vo: And just like Arjun, the turtle spins on its spot. It does not walk. It only changes the way it faces.
beats.caption: It spins on the spot. No walking!

beats.vo: Turn right ninety, four times, and the turtle is back where it started, facing the same way. A full turn!
beats.caption: turn right 90 × 4 = a full turn

beats.vo: In the next chapter, you'll mix turns with steps, to draw shapes. So exciting!
beats.caption: Next chapter: draw shapes with turns!

beats.vo: Okay champ, practice check time, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: You face north. You make two quarter turns right. Which way are you facing now? Pause the video, and try it.
beats.caption: Face north. 2 quarter turns right. Which way?

beats.vo: South! North to east is one turn. East to south is two. Two quarter turns make a half turn, so you face the opposite way. Brilliant!
beats.caption: South! N → E → S is a half turn

beats.vo: Let's remember. Ninety degrees is a quarter turn. One hundred and eighty is a half turn. And three hundred and sixty is a full turn.
beats.caption: 90° quarter · 180° half · 360° full

beats.vo: Four quarter turns bring you all the way back.
beats.caption: 4 quarter turns bring you back

beats.vo: A right turn is clockwise. North, east, south, west.
beats.caption: Right turn = clockwise: N → E → S → W

beats.vo: And a turn changes where you face, not where you stand.
beats.caption: A turn changes where you face

beats.vo: Chapter four, done! You can turn like a coding turtle, champ.
beats.caption: Chapter 4 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
